message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Atomic mass** | ~1.008 u (average of isotopes) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Electronegativity** | 2.20 (Pauling scale) |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈0.00008988 g cm⁻³) |
| **Molecular weight** | 2.016 g mol⁻¹ (H₂) |
| **State at room temperature** | Gas |
| **Isotopes** | ¹H (protium), ²H (deuterium), ³H (tritium) |
| **Bonding** | Forms covalent bonds; diatomic H₂ is the most common form |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; reacts with oxygen to form water (combustion) |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive with many elements; forms hydrides with metals and nonmetals |
| **Acidity/Basicity** | Acts as a weak acid (hydrogen ion donor) in aqueous solutions |
| **Solubility in water** | ~0.0006 g g⁻¹ at 25 °C (very low) |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman, Balmer, Paschen series in UV/visible/IR |
| **Uses** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), industrial hydrogenation, ammonia synthesis (Haber process), rocket propellant, laboratory reagent |

**Key chemical characteristics**

- **Diatomic nature**: Hydrogen naturally exists as H₂ molecules under normal conditions.
- **High ionization energy**: Makes it relatively stable as a neutral atom but highly reactive when ionized.
- **Low density**: Makes it lighter than air; used in balloons and as a lifting gas.
- **Isotopic differences**: Deuterium and tritium have distinct nuclear properties, useful in nuclear fusion research and as tracers in chemistry.

These properties make hydrogen a cornerstone of chemistry, physics, and energy science.
